Samsung is developing 11K displays for their phones
11K is useless if they keep using their "innovative" PenTile for subpixel arrangement.
yeah, but I still want it though
I've gotta be the only person who actually likes PenTile.
How about a longer battery life instead. Rather have that than a display above 4k

I agree. At that size, I am 99% sure it's impossible to tell the difference between 4k and 11k.

A 2 day battery? Now that'd be cool. 11k is just stupid.

I'm pretty sure I can't tell the difference between 1440x2560 and 1080x1920 at 5"-6" screen sizes. I would like to have a battery that lasts more than a day. The Nexus 6, for example, has 443 PPI and the iPhone 6 has 326 PPI (which is the same PPI as the iPhone 4). If the Nexus 6 had a 1080p screen, it would have 370 PPI, well above Apple's baseline. I would have much rather traded those extra 1.6 million pixels for extra battery life.

I cannot imagine why one would need more than 1080p on a sub-16" screen; heck, my Lumia 920 is WXGA(1280 x 768) on a 4.5" screen and I cannot complain.
To clarify I'd rather pay less for the device than have QHD+.
I agree. I have an iPhone 6, and I'd happily downgrade to 260 ppi for a few more hours of battery.
Hmmm, now I wouldn't. Blame Apple for trying to make the phone needlessly thin.

I totally agree on the battery life issue. Higher resolutions eat up battery fast. I have to think this is all to do with better resolutions for vr which I'm not completely opposed to, since even with the s6's resolution vr doesn't look all that great when the phone is an inch from your eye.

I read that, unlike other aspects in technology, batteries have a really high bottleneck in terms of advancement. So, you can't really invent a battery to hold more energy than you can a barrel of oil. I hope someone knows what I'm talking about; There's only so much you can do with batteries.

Sure, but if the best battery out there can power an 11K phone for a whole day, then that same battery could power a 4K phone for a few days. That's the point. I don't need a ridiculous resolution on my phone, but I would like to get throughout the day without having to charge it.

Do we really need an 11K Display? I mean I feel the same about Octa-Core Processors (especially considering the phone will only use one Quad at a time). For Android/Samsung in particular it seems the on-paper specifications vastly exceed what an Android phone really needs. Or does Android actually need all that power?

Android really doesn't need all that power, it's more of a numbers game (We got more cores/RAM/megapixels/whatever than X), dual core phones work perfectly fine. In my opinion Samsung tends to cram more power then what's needed as an excuse to not optimize their Android build. Mobile gaming is the only use for all these high power phones. Although more power is needed to drive higher resolution at 60 fps, I think we are fast approaching diminishing returns on the resolution front. They should work on other things than increasing the resolution.

Exactly, battery seems to be the area which is currently weakest in phones. I work for a phone shop, (and used to work for Samsung too actually), and in each position I notice nobody really knows what to look for on phones, so just try get a phone which trumps everything else for numbers. You have a market of people who snuff a 2.5GHz Quad Core phone for a 2.7GHz Quad Core when all they ever do is take pictures and play Candy Crush.

Do we need an 11k display? Absolutely not. But the fact of the matter is that they know idiots who believe they can tell the difference between 4k and 11k on a 5 inch screen will buy that shit. I'd probably do the same thing if I knew my customers were that dumb. Too many people don't realize pixel density/resolution is like FPS. There is a point where it just doesn't matter anymore.
Besides enhancing speed/power/display/etc, do we have any idea of what the next big step in smart phones will be?

Legislation to stop companies/the government from tracking you and keeping your activity data?

A non-horrible input method (touchscreen is garbage)?

A good OS that doesn't have tons of payware/adware/garbageware?

Smartphones aren't worth having for me until all of these things have been fixed. I don't get why they've become so insanely popular, because their slight convenience isn't worth their problems.
Scamsung coming at ya with another useless "feature."
The resolution is going to be so good it's going to bleed into reality.

Hey Voat. Serious answers, please.

I don't know if I've been living under a rock, or what... but I don't know the first thing about Bitcoin, other than its a form of currency. What's there to know about it?

Apparently Voat accepts Bitcoin donations, PayPal is giving Atko a hard time, etc. I'd like to contribute to Voat somehow, but I've heard a few people say, "I'd stay the f*ck away from Bitcoin". What's the problem with Bitcoin? Is it worth it to get involved if it means that I can help support Voat? If not, what alternative means should Voat seek out in order to accept donations?

Thanks for your answers!
Well bitcoin's value is very unstable and that makes many people not so eager to invest in it.

Bitcoin is an unstable crypto-currency. People are saying you shouldn't put a bunch of your money into a bitcoin wallet since it could devalue at any point. There is a lot to know about it that I do not. The basic thing is that people use computers to solve certain equations and then they get a bitcoin. Also the more bitcoins that are made the more complex those equations get.

Also, just a heads up, there's no need for a serious tag here :) You may get a joke reply or two if you don't put one up, but there will be a majority of voaters that properly answer your question.

Full disclosure, I have never bought/traded bitcoin, all of this is 100% opinion anyone can feel free to correct me.

I think when people say "Stay away" they mean to stay away from bitcoin as an investment. Sure, early bitcoin investors probably had lots of success, but now the currency is no longer unique and the market is too up and down and is not a good long term investment. If all you're looking to do is convert money to bitcoin to make a one time payment you shouldn't have any issues.

While the unstable value point is true, its probably not the reason people are being wary - OP just wants to donate a sum, after all.

The actual "dangerous" part is that the exchanges (that swap your regular currency for Bitcoin) have had a spotty track record in recent times, just look up Mt Gox. Basically a whole bunch of Bitcoin was stolen and despite the whole block-chain deal, some are still unaccounted for. Then of course if you are particular about those sort of things, Bitcoin is often associated with payments for several criminal activities.

That said, if you really just want to donate, I'd say go for it
Bitcoin is unstable - that's its pitfall primarily. Other than that, it's a pretty nifty concept. I have seen its price increase about $70 in the past month.

Bitcoin is a unstable currency and is a risk investment. There are many security flaws in holding and making transaction with Bitcoin and Bitcoin is widely used as a internet black-market currency because of its tax avoidance. Buying some Bitcoin from a credible source and making transactions with credible companies/people should be fine.

Be aware: if you find yourself downvoating this comment, you are caught in an ego trap.

I think the issue is that it is human nature to constantly compare yourself to others and find yourself superior, to prop your own ego up. One of the best (IMHO), simplest (and most common, due to Christian religion) ways to explain it is 'judge not, lest ye be judged'. Let people do their own thing, and you do yours. It's just a constant battle to suppress the ego, though. At least, it is in modern western society. I don't know about other places/areas, but I suspect that ego is a universal driver.

When I see people participating in irresponsible activities, I find myself wanting them to do better. My response is usually to guide or introduce alternatives. Is it egotism to bring others to a more liberating potential? Is my attempt to alter their path in any way a self-righteous action?

This post seems a tad black and white... in fact, it's literally black and white. It seems more of a shaming of those seeking a healthy lifestyle in the face of mass consumerism.

Do not be dismissive of people who do not adhere to your life goals. But do not be a dictator either. You have a voice for a reason, exersize your discretion.
